waarden.prompt:
Create the structure of a slide deck for my talk on {tema|anders:[topic]}.
Objective: {verb} {relatie|bank:wie|anders:your audience}, so that {res|anders:[what changes]}.
Audience: {kwadrant|label|klein|anders:-} ({kwadrant|bank:kort|anders:-}).
Structure: {estr|bank:b1}, {estr|bank:b2}, {estr|bank:b3}.

Rules: one slide per idea, 8 to 12 slides, a short title per slide. Follow the 5/5/5 rule: at most five words per line, five lines per slide and five text-heavy slides in a row. Suggest a visual for each slide. Do not invent data; mark any figure as [data to add].

relatieadvies.peer: You speak to peers: you can be direct, but earn their attention with what they gain, not with your position.
relatieadvies.boven: They decide over your topic: lead with your conclusion and the decision you need, then the support.
relatieadvies.team: They report to you: say why this matters and what you expect of them, then invite their questions.
relatieadvies.buiten: They do not know you yet: say in one sentence who you are and why this matters to them, before the content.

advies.bystanders: They are not keen and know little. Win their attention first: open with what is in it for them. Avoid jargon and give one example per idea.
advies.sceptics: They are not keen but know the subject. Open with what is in it for them, then bring depth: data, nuance and an answer to the objection you expect.
advies.learners: They want to listen but the subject is new to them. Go straight in, build up from the basics and keep the terms simple.
advies.experts: They want to listen and know the subject well. Skip the basics and bring depth, data and nuance.

t1.problem: What pain does your audience feel today?
t1.time: How did we get here? Only what they need to follow you.
t1.why: Why does this matter to your audience?
t1.wsn: What happened, or what is the situation?

t2.problem: Which two or three causes are behind it?
t2.why: How does it work, in a few clear steps?
t2.wsn: Why does it matter to your audience?

t3.problem: What do you propose, and what is the first step?
t3.time: What comes next, and what do we do now?
t3.why: What will be done or decided, and by whom?
t3.wsn: What should happen next, and who does what?

plan.hour:
1. Read your opening and closing aloud three times.
2. Run through the three blocks once, out loud, with a timer.
plan.day:
1. Memorize your full introduction and conclusion.
2. Two run-throughs out loud, with a timer.
3. Rehearse the moves between the blocks separately.
plan.days:
1. Memorize your full introduction and conclusion.
2. One run-through out loud each day, with a timer.
3. Practise once for a colleague and ask what they remember.

resvoorbeeld.Inform: e.g. they know where the project stands
resvoorbeeld.Instruct: e.g. they can log a ticket in the new system
resvoorbeeld.Activate: e.g. they sign up for the pilot
resvoorbeeld.Inspire: e.g. they believe the new strategy can work
